notes: Added for relation-property coverage (CRITERIA Rule 12): a class-membership edit, so its two determinate queries use a declared role chain (instance_of ∘ subclass_of ⊑ instance_of: shark → cartilaginous fish) and ABox inheritance (every shark has a cartilage skeleton). Derivability unlikely: 'dolphins are mammals' is stated thousands of times, but it can also be reached through 'dolphins are toothed whales'. The edit crosses a class boundary on purpose. Determinate vs indeterminate: positive defining traits of the new class (a cartilage skeleton, membership in the cartilaginous fish) are forced on any member, so a by-name belief against them gives way; absences that only generalize over known sharks (no shark nurses, the Act does not cover sharks) can be broken by a new member, so the by-name traits survive in w1. Worlds: two independent storage choices (nursing, the Act), combined into 4 worlds. Dropped: 'Does the dolphin breathe air?' (sharks breathing through gills does not exclude also breathing air, so it was hard to make either answer firm), 'Is the dolphin warm-blooded?' (some sharks, such as the mako, are partly warm-blooded: R1). Names: 海豚 and delfín do not encode the class. Near query: the orca is the largest dolphin whatever dolphins are. Formal check (FINDINGS C1, C4): the side facts the answers rely on are stated: 'no mammal is a cartilaginous fish' (q0 before the edit), 'dolphins have skeletons made of bone' (q1 before the edit; it gives way in every world, listed in each world), 'no shark nurses its young' (q2's w2 and w4 chains; it gives way in w1 and w3), 'dolphins are marine animals' (q3), and the Act's coverage by description reads 'every marine mammal, and only marine mammals' (w2 and w3 answer no once the dolphin is not a mammal).
